source: Jhaveri, GX-Chen, Sucholutsky, Choi (2026) Failing to Falsify: confirmation bias in language models
finding: Wason 2-4-6 style rule discovery with 11 LLMs. Models often test triples that fit their current hypothesis instead of triples that could break it. Success varied widely by model.
numbers: Success 6% to 78% across models within 45 turns. Human-derived prompts raised mean rule-discovery rate from 42% to 56%.
limits: Integer-triple task with LLM-written rules. Not a direct Kuhn test: it tests hypothesis-testing policy, not frame replacement.
agent_relevance: Models do not self-generate disconfirming tests. A schema should force counterexample tests in code (supports G1/G3), not rely on the model to doubt.

source: Jhaveri, GX-Chen, Sucholutsky, Choi (2026) Failing to Falsify: confirmation bias in language models (Table 2, Qwen3 family)
finding: Thinking mode raised success but not by lowering confirmation bias. Incompatible:compatible test ratio (I:C) correlated with success.
numbers: Qwen3-8B baseline success 0.06 (non-thinking) vs 0.21 (thinking); Qwen3-32B 0.33 vs 0.41. I:C for thinking baselines 0.14 to 0.32. 80 episodes per cell. I:C correlates with success in both groups, stronger for thinking models.
limits: 80 test episodes per cell: wide intervals. 4 test rule sets only.
agent_relevance: More reasoning tokens does not equal more falsification. Count the falsifying-test rate in code as a signal.

source: Jhaveri, GX-Chen, Sucholutsky, Choi (2026) Failing to Falsify: confirmation bias in language models (interventions)
finding: Think-in-Opposites prompt improved success in all 11 model-mode scenarios. Dual-Goal improved 8 of 11. Gains significant for thinking models, mixed for non-thinking.
numbers: Qwen3-8B thinking 0.21 to 0.40 with TiO; Qwen3-32B thinking 0.41 to 0.61; Llama-3.3-70B 0.21 to 0.38 with TiO. Dual-Goal hurt non-thinking Qwen3-14B (0.23 to 0.13) and Qwen3-32B (0.33 to 0.10). I:C rose in 18 of 22 cases.
limits: Prompt-based; non-thinking models can be harmed. Small N.
agent_relevance: A 'seek the opposite' operator helps strong reasoners but can hurt weak ones. Gate by model strength; test before adding.

source: Jhaveri, GX-Chen, Sucholutsky, Choi (2026) Failing to Falsify: confirmation bias in language models (distillation and transfer)
finding: Fine-tuning on the lower-bias behaviour put it into the model without a prompt, and part of it transferred to the Blicket test.
numbers: Qwen3-8B + 8B TiO distillation: success 0.21 to 0.35, I:C 0.15 to 0.31. Cross-scale plus intervention (8B student, 32B TiO teacher) 0.59, I:C 0.38.
limits: Needs training, outside our no-training constraint. Transfer tested on one new task.
agent_relevance: The policy gap is shallow and promptable; we get it by scaffold, not training.

source: Bertolazzi et al. (2026) FalsifyBench: rule-discovery games for hypothesis testing and belief revision
finding: 12 LLMs play 100 WordNet games (max 20 turns) as player and oracle. Share of positive (confirming) tests strongly predicts failure.
numbers: Success: GPT-5.2-Chat 75%, GPT-OSS-120B 68%, DeepSeek-V3.1 41%, other instruction-tuned 33-35%, GPT-5-Nano 12%. Confirmation bias vs success rho -0.779 (p=0.003); vs conclusive falsification rate rho -0.937. Mixed-effects n=1,200 games: OR 0.016 for confirmation bias; oracle error OR 0.885 (no effect). Instruction-tuned positive-test share 66-82%.
limits: No interventions tested. Belief revision measured by proxies only. English WordNet only. Last 1,041 characters of page unread.
agent_relevance: Failure is the model's test choice, not oracle noise. Failed games show anchoring on surface features (spelling, syllables): 97.6% of failed GLM-5 games. A code check on whether a test separates hypotheses is warranted.

source: Alignment Forum post (2025) LLM rule-discovery Numberwang pilot
finding: 11 LLMs, 10 rules drawn from 60, up to 19 rounds. Models often did not falsify; some added special cases (epicycles) when contrary evidence arrived instead of dropping the hypothesis.
numbers: Mean success 11%, median 10%; 4 of 11 models got 0 rules; o1-preview 3 of 10; Claude 3.6 Sonnet 4 of 10 (30% on two reruns). About 25% of responses were invalid JSON.
limits: Informal blog, not peer reviewed. Prompt tuned mostly on one model. Judge was a model.
agent_relevance: Direct match to Kuhn and Lakatos: patching a failing theory. A signal counting patches per hypothesis could trigger S6.

source: Li et al. (2025) Patterns Over Principles: fragility of inductive reasoning in LLMs under noisy observations (ACL Findings)
finding: Robust Rule Induction on arithmetic, cryptography and list functions. LLMs show hypothesis drift and pattern overfitting under noisy examples. Accuracy can stay flat while consistency falls.
numbers: Abstract only: slight accuracy variation, with one case of 0 accuracy change and a consistency score of only 70. Sample-steered Rule Refinement (SRR) degrades least under noise. No per-level numbers on the page.
limits: Only the abstract page was opened, not the PDF.
agent_relevance: Noise looks like anomaly: one failure should not trigger a frame switch. Supports requiring several independent failures (Kuhn crisis threshold).

source: Haq et al. (2025) Is your LLM trapped in a Mental Set?
finding: Einstellung-style test (DeCaro 2016 mathematical equivalence). In-context examples raised exact match but did not change the number of steps. Zero-shot chain of thought raised steps per problem.
numbers: Few-shot exact match: GPT-4o 0.33 (shortcut) to 0.66 with complex-first; Llama-3.1-70B 0 to 0.66 on complex problems with shortcut-first. Steps with few-shot: 1; with few-shot plus CoT: 3 in every cell. Six problems per condition.
limits: Six problems per cell, three models, one task: anecdotal. Humans need 1 step; authors read 3 steps as CoT-induced set.
agent_relevance: Rigidity (mental set) is a light cousin of paradigm lock-in. Evidence is weak; cite as a hint only [S].

source: Zhang et al. (2025) NewtonBench: scientific law discovery with metaphysical shifts
finding: 324 law-discovery tasks over 12 physics domains; laws altered so memory cannot answer. Capability is uneven and falls with system complexity and noise.
numbers: Symbolic accuracy without code: GPT-5 72.9%, Gemini-2.5-pro 65.0%, o4-mini 47.5%, DeepSeek-V3 9.7%, GPT-4.1 5.3%. GPT-5 on complex-system hard: 29.9%. Noise 0.0001 cut GPT-5-mini accuracy 13-15%.
limits: Four runs per setting, temperature 0.4; LLM judge. Last 55,890 characters unread.
agent_relevance: Altered-law tasks are the closest benchmark to a new-paradigm-needed case. Noise sensitivity means thresholds must be robust.

source: NewtonBench code-tool finding
finding: A code interpreter helped weak models and hurt strong ones. Authors attribute this to a premature shift from exploring to exploiting (satisficing).
limits: Explanation is correlational; no exact exploration rates in the text.
agent_relevance: Tools that make a good-enough fit easy can freeze the frame early. Guard with held-out checks (G3).

source: Wiemann et al. (2026) DiscoverPhysics: interactive discovery of non-standard physics
finding: 22 worlds (Yukawa gravity, hidden particles, time-varying couplings). Prediction and explanation decouple: a model can fit well while its stated law is wrong.
numbers: pass@1/pass@5: claude-opus-4-7 26.4/50.0; gpt-5.5 21.7/36.4; Qwen3.5-397B 4.5/9.1; claude-sonnet-4-6 1.8/9.1; haiku-4-5 0.0/0.0. Explanation score 0.61 (opus) vs 0.10 (Llama-3.3-70B). Five seeds per world; 5% noise.
limits: Judge is a Claude model (self-preference risk); pass thresholds arbitrary; curated small worlds. Table values may be garbled by extraction.
agent_relevance: Authors read gpt-5.5 as locking in a law and tuning parameters instead of revising the concept: normal science inside a failing paradigm. Predictive fit alone must not stop the loop.

source: EvoSCM (2026) Scientific belief revision through causal model evolution (Hugging Face summary page)
finding: Keeps several competing causal models. Each makes a falsifiable prediction before each experiment. Recurring discrepancies become correction rules. Revision prefers shallow edits and uses structural edits only when needed.
numbers: GPT-5.4 pass@1 1.86% to 38.08%; pass@5 9.09% to 54.55%. GPT-5.5 pass@1 7.25% to 53.04%; pass@5 27.27% to 63.64%. Qwen3.6 baseline 0% at all k; with injected models pass@1 14.95% to 39.85%.
limits: Baseline prompt not fully specified; trials per pass@k not given; only the summary page was read.
agent_relevance: Closest working analogue of an S6 trigger: recurring prediction failures lead to ordered revision (parameter, mechanism, structure). The rival-model population echoes Kuhn and Lakatos rival programmes.

source: Alderete et al. (2026) Separable Pathways for Causal Reasoning (Extended Blicket Benchmark)
finding: Hidden moderator: the rule flips from conjunctive to disjunctive after N activations. A runtime monitor that detects the regime change and expands the hypothesis space stops premature answers.
numbers: 1,085 trials, Claude Sonnet 4.5. Hard post-switch rule (n=50 per agent): reasoning-eligible accuracy Base 73.3%, context graph 93.9%, plus dynamic behaviours 95.3%. Exactly-N early submission 28.0% to 6.0% (p=0.003). Rule-change detector sensitivity 100%, PPV 90.5-100%. Stochastic (p=0.70) condition: all agents 73-77%, no advantage.
limits: Single model family; last 33,768 characters unread; cost about 807 USD.
agent_relevance: Evidence for a code-run anomaly monitor that adds a state meaning the rule has changed. Boundary: in noisy worlds the monitor gave no gain, so thresholds need noise handling.

source: Rios-Garcia et al. (2026) AI scientists produce results without reasoning scientifically (via Science News)
finding: 619 chemistry reasoning tasks with step-level annotation, 3 LLMs in 2 agent designs. Agents rarely revise hypotheses when evidence contradicts them.
numbers: Ignored evidence at least once in 68% of tasks; made claims without supporting evidence in 53%; used contradictory evidence to change output in 26%.
limits: Secondary news report; the arXiv paper itself not opened. Models unnamed.
agent_relevance: Base rate for failure to revise: about three in four tasks show no revision after contradiction. Strong case for code-forced revision on a failed check (G2).

source: LongChang (2026) Can LLMs uncover hidden physical laws through free exploration? arXiv 2610.37649
finding: 15 altered-physics scenes, up to 100 turns, 12 LLMs with no task hint. Noticing and chasing an anomaly was rare. Only one model made any discovery.
numbers: Discovery rate: top model 16.7%, all others 0.0% (Claude-Opus-5 law correctness 16.7% but evidence support 0.0%). Task guidance 16.7% to 28.6%; 500-turn budget 14.3% (no gain). 36.1% of reports on normal-physics controls were rejected for false anomaly claims.
limits: Model names are as the page printed them; I could not cross-check them, so treat numbers with caution. Judge and best explorer may share a family.
agent_relevance: Two failure sides: missing real anomalies and inventing false ones (36.1%). An anomaly trigger needs a control comparison, not the model's say-so.

source: Gandhi et al. (2025) BoxingGym
finding: 10 environments for experimental design and model revision. Giving the agent prior domain information often did not help: it made strong assumptions and did not revise them after more experiments.
numbers: Six LLMs; 32B models beat 7B in each family; in the hyperbolic-discounting environment error rose with more experiments. Prior info often worse after 10 experiments (Fig. 3a).
limits: Per-model scores are in figures I could not read as text.
agent_relevance: A strong prior frame can hurt: it resists revision. Argues for logging the frame and its failures explicitly.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) DuSAR: co-adaptive dual-strategy framework (Strategy Fitness Score)
finding: A frozen LLM holds a global plan and a local policy; a fitness score of the current strategy decides when to revise the global plan.
numbers: ALFWorld 37.1% with Llama3.1-70B vs prior best 13.0%; Mind2Web 4.02%; per-step tokens cut 3 to 9 times.
limits: Abstract page only; ablation of the trigger not seen.
agent_relevance: A working switch-when-fitness-drops trigger in an agent loop. Check how the threshold was chosen before copying.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion
finding: Verbal reflection on failure carried into the next trial. This is retry with a lesson, not a frame switch.
numbers: 91% pass@1 on HumanEval vs 80% for GPT-4 (abstract).
limits: Only the abstract was read. AlfWorld and HotPotQA numbers seen in a search snippet were not verified.
agent_relevance: Baseline for revise after failure. Our S6 adds a different step: replace the frame after several independent failures, not only reflect.

source: Understanding Data blog (2025) Clean slate trajectory recovery
finding: Practitioner rule: after 3 or more failed attempts with a repeated approach, restart in a fresh context that carries only the lessons.
numbers: Scenario figures (about 30% vs 80% success) are labeled illustrative, not measured.
limits: No study or dataset behind it. Blog heuristic.
agent_relevance: The 3-failure threshold is a folk number with no measurement. We should measure it ourselves [D].

source: Cross-domain benchmarks (2026) coordinated agents, with a Computational Kuhn task, arXiv 2605.22300
finding: Retrospective detection of 16 historical paradigm shifts against 16 matched controls from citation, semantic-drift and funding features. Citation features did nearly all the work.
numbers: Full coordinated workflow AUROC 0.9688, pairwise accuracy 0.9375, median lead 3.0 years, calibration error 0.6243. Single-agent summary 0.969; scripted bibliometrics 0.969; citation-only 0.969; semantic-only 0.844; funding-only 0.531.
limits: Retrospective, summary-level features, 16 pairs; not prospective forecasting. Coordination gave no AUROC gain.
agent_relevance: Kuhn crises are detectable from counted features in a literature, which suggests counted signals, not model judgement, for our trigger.

source: Kuhn (1962) The Structure of Scientific Revolutions
finding: Normal science solves puzzles inside a paradigm; anomalies pile up; crisis; a rival paradigm replaces it. Anomalies alone do not force a switch: a rival must exist and fit better.
numbers: From memory; no numbers.
limits: Not re-read this session. Historians dispute how well the pattern fits real episodes; Kuhn gave no threshold for enough anomalies.
agent_relevance: Source of the S6 idea. The theory has no count threshold, so ours must be tuned [D].

source: Lakatos (1970) Falsification and the methodology of scientific research programmes
finding: A programme is degenerating when it only adds ad hoc patches after the facts; progressive when it predicts new facts. Replace a programme only when a rival does better.
numbers: From memory; no numbers.
limits: Not opened. Philosophy, no empirical test.
agent_relevance: Operational test for the agent: count patches and novel predictions per frame; patch-only growth is the switch signal. Matches the epicycle finding (c06).

source: Langley, Simon, Bradshaw, Zytkow (1987) Scientific Discovery: BACON and successors
finding: Older computational discovery systems rediscovered laws by search over data, without anomaly-driven frame switching beyond trying new term combinations.
numbers: From memory; BACON rediscovered laws such as Kepler's third law from data.
limits: Not opened; details unchecked.
agent_relevance: Historical baseline: law-fitting search is old; the new part is knowing when to drop a frame.

source: Thagard (1992) Conceptual Revolutions: explanatory coherence model ECHO
finding: Computational model of theory change: a rival theory wins when it explains more evidence with more coherence, modelling revolutions as a network settling.
numbers: From memory; no numbers.
limits: Not opened; claim not verified here.
agent_relevance: A code-level way to compare frames: coherence score over evidence, not a model's opinion.

source: Bertolazzi et al. (2026) FalsifyBench (failure pattern line)
finding: Failed games had more turns where the hypothesis only partly overlapped the target, and many hypotheses rested on surface features. Models stayed on a partly right frame.
numbers: Partial-overlap turns higher in failed games: GPT-5.2-Chat +27.0 pp, GPT-OSS-120B +22.3 pp, GLM-5 +21.4 pp. Surface-feature hypotheses in 97.6% of failed GLM-5 games, 92.0% GPT-5.2-Chat, 84.4% GPT-OSS-120B. Not significant for GPT-5-Nano and Qwen3.5-9B.
limits: Human annotation covered only one Test and one Guess turn per game.
agent_relevance: Near-miss frames are the trap: a partly right frame feels like progress. A switch rule should look at failed checks, not at similarity to the target.
